description:
Doubler Aerospace — Analog Site Pack

Canadian aerospace startup (Phase 01: CAD & DFM). Earth analog sites for Moon-base and Mars conditions, paired with test hardware: fixtures, mockup frames, mounts, dust/thermal stands. NASA open data, site scoring, DFM briefs. Canada-first + global.
summary:
TerraAnalog AI is an interactive decision-support platform that ranks Earth analog sites for testing lunar and Martian mission hardware, procedures, and crews. A user selects one of 14 lunar or Martian reference regions and one of 11 mission objectives; the app then ranks 28 terrestrial sites on an interactive globe. Each ranking is a transparent score built from 11 reference-specific similarity features, drawn from 4,340 research records (measured, modeled or provisional values, plus 378 explicitly missing ones), together with evidence completeness, confidence, a source for every value, and an explicit list of what Earth cannot replicate.

Missing evidence lowers completeness instead of being filled in. Users can inspect sources, re-weight criteria, stress-test rankings, compare sites, and export CSV or PDF reports. The scoring engine is deterministic and explainable, not a generative model, and it reproduces all 588 published research rankings (maximum score difference under 0.0001 points, 0 rank mismatches). The project addresses the challenge of using Earth as a testbed for the Moon and Mars by making analog-site choice auditable, evidence-based, and reusable through an open data contract.
details:
TerraAnalog AI is an interactive decision-support platform for choosing terrestrial analog sites. A user picks one of 14 lunar or Martian reference regions and one of 11 mission objectives. The application then ranks 28 Earth sites on an interactive globe and shows a transparent score for each one.

How it works. Eleven reference-specific similarity features (lithology, process, landform, resource, slope, ruggedness, thermal, aridity, ice/permafrost, abiotic surface, and fine sediment) are scored against the selected reference. A separate operational-suitability score is shown but is never mixed into analog fidelity. Weights combine the target body, the reference, the mission objective, and any weights the user sets in the Custom Weight Lab. The research contract holds 4,340 feature records: 770 measured, 1,519 modeled and 1,673 provisional values, plus 378 missing values. Missing values are not imputed; they lower evidence completeness, and the score is shown as a range rather than a false single number. Each value is tied to a source and can be opened in the evidence inspector. The recommendation engine parses a plain-language request into structured filters and the same documented score; it is deterministic and cannot invent sites, citations, or measurements. Users can compare up to four sites, run sensitivity and cluster analyses, and export a CSV or a server-generated PDF report, or share a deep link to the same view.

Benefits and intended impact. The platform makes analog-site choice faster to explore and easier to audit, with sources, completeness, confidence, and Earth’s hard limits (gravity, vacuum or a CO2 atmosphere, radiation, and permanently shadowed-region cryogenics) kept in view. The intended users are mission and field teams planning tests of hardware, procedures, or crews, as well as educators. An open nine-file data contract means a new research export can update the whole platform without code changes.

Tools and languages. The interface is Next.js, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, MapLibre GL, deck.gl, and Recharts. The scoring API is FastAPI (Python), with PDF export via ReportLab. The stack runs locally, in Docker Compose, or as two web services on Render.

Creativity. Rankings are specific to a named planetary reference and a stated objective, not a generic “Mars-like” list. Completeness, confidence, value type, and non-replicable factors are first-class parts of the result. Judges can re-weight criteria live and see ranks move, and can inspect every source.

Factors considered. Explainable scoring was required; a runtime language model was not, because it could invent facts. Data gaps are disclosed rather than filled in. Licences and attribution for each dataset are recorded in the catalog and on the Data & Provenance page. Planetary coordinates use the Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature and IAU body radii, not WGS84 on the Moon or Mars. Analog scores are decision-support proxies: they are not landing-site selections and not flight-hardware qualification.

Quality (pre-submission audit, 15 November 2026; GitHub Actions passing on the final commit): 97 backend tests, 25 frontend unit tests and 50 desktop, mobile, keyboard and accessibility end-to-end checks passed, plus a production build. The data audit passes 17 of 17 checks with 0 validation errors. All 588 published rankings are reproduced (maximum score difference 0.00004737 points, 0 rank mismatches).

Use of AI: Grok Bot, Cursor and ChatGPT/Codex helped write code, documentation and data-processing scripts under the team's direction. The deployed app uses no generative AI at runtime, and all screenshots are real captures, not AI-generated.

Live app: https://terraanalog-web-cqgu.onrender.com

Source code: https://github.com/ThynkAI/terraanalog-ai
